source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} the disciples{H8527} drew near{H7126} to Yeshua{H3442} and said{H559} to him: Whom{H4310} do you think{H2803} great{H1419} in the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}?

greek_deviations: The disciples ask whom YESHUA thinks great — מי אתה חושב, 'whom do YOU think' — where Greek Matthew has the impersonal 'who then is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?' The Hebrew question seeks his judgment, not a ranking.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״ז (Perek 77) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (18:1): ויאמרו...חושב] ויאמר אליהם אתם חושבים G; אל ישו] לישו G.

verses.translation: And he called{H7121} one{H259} small{H6996} lad{H5288} and set him{H7760} in their midst{H8432}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:2): 'By haplography (נער אחד...נער אחד) all our mss, except A, omit 18:2b-5a. The text printed above in parentheses is according to ms A, which contains all but vs 4.' The parenthesis in Howard's print opens before קטן here and closes after נער א׳ in v. 5: everything between the two occurrences of נער אחד fell out of the whole family except ms A, whose text Howard prints in parentheses.

verses.translation: And he said{H559}: I say{H559}, if you do not turn{H7725} to be like this{H2088} lad{H5288}, you will not enter{H935} the kingdom of heaven.

one_way_hebrew: תשובו (H7725, shuv) — 'unless you TURN': the prophets' word for repentance (teshuvah, Hos 14:2-3, שובה ישראל). Greek στραφῆτε translates the same call; in Hebrew the noun teshuvah is already living in the verb.
במ״ש — the ms abbreviates מלכות שמים as במ״ש, exactly as a Hebrew scribe abbreviates a running rabbinic phrase (malkhut shamayim); a translator from Greek does not abbreviate his own renderings.
textual_notes: Part of the ms-A parenthetical section (see v. 2 note).

Greek 18:4 ('whoever humbles himself as this little child...') has no counterpart here: even ms A, which alone preserves this section, lacks v. 4; the text runs from v. 3 to v. 5. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries v. 4 ('he who will humble himself like this boy will be great in the heavenly kingdom').

verses.translation: And he who receives{H6901} one{H259} lad{H5288} like this{H2088} in my name{H8034}, receives{H6901} me.

translation_notes: The base text ends at מקבל ('receives —'); ms A adds אותי ('me'), and Howard's English supplies '(me).' The sense requires it and the translation follows.
א׳ — the ms abbreviation for אחד ('one'), as at 16:14.
textual_notes: Howard's parenthetical A-text section closes after נער א׳ here (see v. 2 note).
Howard's apparatus (18:5): כזה] בזה EFG; מקבל] + אותי A.

verses.translation: And he who causes one{H259} of the small{H6996} lads{H5288} who believe{H539} in me to stumble{H3782} — it is good{H2896} for him that he tie{H7194} a piece{H6400} of an upper millstone{H7393} on his neck{H6677} and be cast{H2904} into the depths{H4688} of the sea{H3220}.

one_way_hebrew: פלח רכב — 'a piece of an upper millstone': Judg 9:53 verbatim (פלח רכב), the millstone-piece a woman dropped on Abimelech's skull (cf. 2 Sam 11:21); רכב is Deut 24:6's upper millstone. Greek μύλος ὀνικός ('donkey-millstone') describes the machine; the Hebrew quotes the Tanakh's own millstone-death.

ויוטל במצולות ים — 'cast into the depths of the sea': Mic 7:19's consonants (ותשליך במצלות ים כל חטאתם — 'you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea'). The offender goes where Micah says the sins go. Greek καταποντισθῇ ἐν τῷ πελάγει τῆς θαλάσσης translates; the Hebrew quotes — and טול (H2904) is Jonah's storm-verb (הטילו, Jonah 1:12,15).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:6): יכשיל] יכשל BDG; מהנערים] מן הנערים DG; הקטנים] omit EF; פלח] פלס CG; על צוארו] בצוארו A; במצולות] במצולת BDG.

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to the inhabitants{H3427} of the world{H8398} because of the confusions{H3998}, for the confusions must{H6878} come{H935}. And he said{H559}: Woe to the man{H120} who comes because of it.

one_way_hebrew: מבוכה (H3998) — 'confusion, entanglement': Isa 22:5's word for the day of trouble and treading-down (מבוכה) and Mic 7:4's, where the watchmen's day brings מבוכתם. Greek σκάνδαλα ('stumbling-blocks') is one figure; the Hebrew names the day-of-the-LORD panic by the prophets' term.
תבל (H8398) — the inhabited world of Ps 24:1; Greek κόσμος translates it.
textual_notes: The first sentence stands in parentheses in Howard's print: his apparatus reads 'אוי...לבא] omit British Library MS and C. Text printed in parentheses is according to A.' The base ms lost the woe-saying by homoioteleuton (אוי...אוי); ms A preserves it.
Howard's apparatus (18:7): שיבא] שיבאו A; תבל] תפל D; אוי²] + לו D.

verses.translation: And if your hand{H3027} or your foot{H7272} causes you to stumble{H3782}, cut it off{H3772} and cast it from you: better{H2896} for you to enter{H935} into life{H2416} blind or lame{H6455} than, having two hands{H3027} and two feet{H7272}, to be given{H5414} to the everlasting{H5769} fire{H784}.

one_way_hebrew: עור או פסח — 'blind or lame': the fixed Tanakh pair (2 Sam 5:8; Lev 21:18) — the Hebrew reaches for its own idiom-pair where Greek has 'maimed or lame' (κυλλὸν ἢ χωλόν).
אש עולמית — 'everlasting fire': the question of Isa 33:14, 'who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings (מוקדי עולם)?'
translation_notes: עוד — the base ms writes עוד; mss ABDEFG read עור ('blind'), which the sense requires (ד/ר confusion), and Howard's English prints '(blind).' The translation follows.
ותכשילהו — the base ms repeats the stumbling-verb ('and make it stumble from you'); ms B reads ותשליכהו ('and cast it from you'), which the sense requires and the translation follows.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:8): עוד] עור ABDEFG; ותכשילהו] ותשליכהו B; ידך] ידיך A; ורגלך] ורגליך A; לתתך] ולתתך A.

verses.translation: And if your eye{H5869} causes you to stumble{H3782}, pluck it out{H5365} and cast it{H7993} from you: better{H2896} for you to enter{H935} into life{H2416} with one{H259} eye{H5869} than, having two eyes, to be given{H5414} into Gehinnom{H1516}.

one_way_hebrew: ותקרה — from נקר (H5365), the eye-gouging verb of Scripture: Samson (ויקרו את עיניו, Judg 16:21), Zedekiah (2 Kgs 25:7), and Nahash's threat (1 Sam 11:2). Greek ἔξελε ('take it out') is bland; the Hebrew uses the verb whose every biblical occurrence is an eye.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:9): ותקרה] נקרהו A, נקרה BDEFG, ונקרה C; ותשליכה] ותשליכהו A; עיניך] עינך BCDEF; אחד] אחת BDG; בגהינם] בגיהנם BDE.

verses.translation: And take care{H2094} lest{H6435} you judge{H1777} one{H259} of the small{H6996} lads{H5288}. I say{H559} to you: their messengers{H4397} continually{H8548} see{H7200} the sons{H1121} of my Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064}.

greek_deviations: Two readings against the Greek in one verse. (1) 'Take care lest you JUDGE (תדינו) one of the small lads' — Greek has 'see that you do not DESPISE (καταφρονήσητε) one of these little ones': the Hebrew forbids sitting in judgment on the small, not merely looking down on them. (2) The base text reads 'their messengers continually see THE SONS of my Father' (בני אבי) — the watchers watch the children — where mss ABCDEFG read פני ('the FACE of my Father') with the Greek. Howard's English keeps the base: 'their angels always see the sons of my father.'
translation_notes: הם רואים — the scan of Howard's text reads הם רואים ('they see'); the circulating transcription's רושים is a garble, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:10): אחת] אחד BDG, א׳ A; מהנערים] מן הנערים D; למלאכיהם] שמלאכיהם A, שמלאכי BEF; בני] פני ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: And the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} has ceased{H988} to save{H3467} the enemies{H341}.

greek_deviations: A doubly strange verse. Greek Matthew 18:11 — itself missing from the earliest Greek witnesses — reads 'the Son of Man came to save THE LOST (τὸ ἀπολωλός).' The Hebrew base reads 'the Son of Man HAS CEASED (בטל) to save THE ENEMIES (האויבים).' Mss BDEFG read בא ('has come') for בטל, and האויבים differs from האובדים ('the lost, the perishing') by a single letter — read with those two small changes, the verse is Luke 19:10's 'came to save the lost.' As printed, Howard renders it straight: 'the Son of Man has stopped saving the enemy.' The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew lacks the verse entirely, with the early Greek witnesses.
translation_notes: The translation renders the base text as printed; the sheep-parable that follows (vv. 12-14) speaks of the נדחה, the driven-away one — the neighbor of האובדים, not האויבים.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:11): בטל] בא BDEFG, omit A; האויבים] את האויבים G.

verses.translation: What{H4100} do you think{H7200}? If a man{H376} has a hundred{H3967} sheep{H6629} and one{H259} of them flies off{H6524}, will he not leave{H5800} the ninety{H8673}-nine{H8672} on the mountains{H2022} and go{H1980} to seek{H1245} the one driven away{H5080}?

one_way_hebrew: הנדחה — 'the DRIVEN-AWAY one': Ezekiel's shepherd-word, the very term of the shepherd chapter — 'I will seek the lost and bring back the driven-away (הנדחת)' (Ezek 34:16; cf. Mic 4:6; Zeph 3:19; Deut 30:4). Greek πλανώμενον ('straying') is the wanderer; the Hebrew נדחה is the one pushed out — Ezekiel 34's own case against the shepherds, which this parable enacts.
translation_notes: ופרח — 'and one of them flies off' (פרח, the bird-verb); mss ABCDEFG read וברח ('flees'), and Howard's English prints '(runs off).'
מאה צאן, יעזוב, ותשעה — so the scan; the circulating transcription's מצאן, יעוזב, and ותשענ are typos, corrected here.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״ח (Perek 78) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (18:12): אחת] אחד DG; ופרח] וברח ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: And if he finds it{H4672}, amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you that he rejoices{H8055} over it more{H3148} than over the ninety{H8673}-nine{H8672} which were not driven away{H5080}.

one_way_hebrew: נדחו — the parable stays inside Ezek 34's vocabulary: the ninety-nine are those 'not driven away.' Greek switches to μὴ πεπλανημένοις ('not gone astray').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:13): אשר לא] שלא A; ותשעה] ותשע A.

verses.translation: So{H3651} the Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064} does not desire{H7521} that one{H259} of the lads{H5288} should be lost{H6}.

one_way_hebrew: שיאבד — 'that one be LOST' (אבד): with v. 12's נדחה, the verse completes Ezek 34:16's pair — 'I will seek THE LOST (האבדת) and bring back THE DRIVEN-AWAY (הנדחת).' The Hebrew parable runs on Ezekiel's two participles; the Greek has neither.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:14): אב] אבי ABCEF ('MY Father,' which Howard's English prints as '(my)'), האב DG; שיאבד] שידחו EF.

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to Shimon{H8095}, called{H7121} Petros: If your brother{H251} sins{H2398} against you, rebuke him{H3198} between him and you{H996}; if he listens{H8085} to you, you have acquired{H7069} your brother{H251}.

one_way_hebrew: הוכיחנו — Lev 19:17's own command: 'you shall surely rebuke (הוכח תוכיח) your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.' Greek ἔλεγξον translates it; the Hebrew halakha of private rebuke stands here in Leviticus' verb, with Leviticus' logic (rebuke instead of resentment).

קנית את אחיך — 'you have ACQUIRED your brother' (קנה, the acquisition verb of Gen 4:1; Prov 4:5-7, 'acquire wisdom'); Greek ἐκέρδησας ('gained') is mercantile, קנה is covenantal — Proverbs' verb for gaining what is most worth having.
greek_deviations: The instruction is addressed to a named man: 'Yeshua said TO SHIMON, CALLED PETROS' — Greek Matthew has no addressee. The community's discipline procedure is handed to the same Shimon who received the keys and the binding-loosing at 16:18-19; v. 18 below then repeats the bind/loose grant in the plural.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading (Perek 79) begins here; the scan's heading is misprinted פקר ע״ט for פרק ע״ט.
Howard's apparatus (18:15): פייטרוס] פיטרו A, פיטרוש BDEFG; הוכיחנו] הוכיחהו D.

verses.translation: And if he does not listen{H8085} to you, rebuke him{H3198} before{H6440} another{H312}; and if with all{H3605} these{H428} he does not listen to you, add{H3254} still one{H259} or two{H8147}, so that it be before two or three{H7969} witnesses{H5707} — for by the mouth{H6310} of two or three witnesses{H5707} a matter{H1697} is established{H6965}.

one_way_hebrew: שעל פי שנים או שלשה עדים יקום דבר — Deut 19:15 in its own consonants (על פי שני עדים או על פי שלשה עדים יקום דבר). The Greek quotes the verse in Greek; the Hebrew text simply continues in the Torah's words — no seam between speech and Scripture.
translation_notes: בכל אלה — the unpointed אלה reads both 'these' (elleh) and 'oath' (alah, H423); Howard renders 'if by every OATH he does not listen.' The translation keeps the plain 'with all these'; the oath-reading recurs in v. 18.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:16): לפנים שנים] omit G; לפנים] לפני BCDEF, להיות דבריך לפני A ('in order that your words might be before,' which Howard's English follows in parentheses); תוסיף] הסוף A; אליך] לך A; עדים¹...עדים²] haplography CD; דבר] הדבר B.

verses.translation: And if with all{H3605} these{H428} he does not listen{H8085}, tell{H559} it in the assembly{H6951}; and if he does not listen in the assembly{H6951}, regard{H2803} him as one banned — an enemy{H341} and a cruel one{H393}.

one_way_hebrew: כמנודה — 'as one BANNED': the menudeh, the man under the rabbinic ban (niddui) — the synagogue's own discipline category, a living halakhic institution. Greek Matthew has 'let him be to you as THE GENTILE AND THE TAX-COLLECTOR (ὁ ἐθνικὸς καὶ ὁ τελώνης).' A Hebrew author writes the court's actual sentence; the Greek substitutes social outsiders for the legal status.

קהל (H6951) — 'the assembly': where Greek Matthew says ἐκκλησία here, the Hebrew has the Torah's קהל (Deut 23:2-9, the assembly one may be barred from — exactly the menudeh's situation). And at 16:18, where Greek also says ἐκκλησία, this text has בית תפלתי: the Hebrew distinguishes the covenant assembly from the house of prayer; the Greek collapses both into one borrowed word.
אכזר (H393) — Job's and Proverbs' word for the cruel (Job 30:21; Prov 11:17; 12:10).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:17): בקהל¹...בקהל²] haplography B.

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you: every one of these{H428} which you bind{H631} on earth{H776} is bound{H631} in heaven{H8064}, and all that you loose{H5425} on earth will be loosed{H5425} in heaven.

one_way_hebrew: תאסרו... תתירו — here the binding-loosing grant is given in the halakhic pair itself, אסר/התיר (issur/hetter) — to forbid and to permit — the everyday working verbs of a Hebrew court; at 16:19 the same grant to Shimon used קשר/התיר. And אסר is Num 30's own vow-binding verb (לאסר אסר, Num 30:3ff): read with Howard's construal of אלה as 'oath' (alah, H423 — 'every OATH which you bind on earth'), the verse is Numbers 30's oath-and-annulment law handed to the community. Both readings stand in the unpointed consonants; either way the idiom is the Hebrew court's, and the Greek δέω/λύω translates it.
The grant here is plural (תאסרו, 'you' all) where 16:19's was singular to Shimon — the Hebrew text keeps the two scopes distinct.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:18): אלה] omit ABDEFG; אסור הוא] transposed G; אשר¹] omit C.

verses.translation: And also{H1571} I say{H559} to you: if two{H8147} of you desire{H7521} to set{H7760} peace{H7965} on earth{H776}, all{H3605} that they seek{H1245} will be yours from Him who is in heaven{H8064}.

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew reads 'if two of you AGREE (συμφωνήσωσιν) on earth about anything they ask'; the Hebrew reads 'if two of you desire TO SET PEACE (לשים שלום) on earth.' The promise is not to unanimity but to peacemaking — and the Greek συμφωνέω ('sound together, be in harmony') reads like a rendering of exactly this shalom-idiom. The condition of answered asking is the making of peace between the two — following directly on the reconciliation procedure of vv. 15-17.
translation_notes: שלים — the ms spells שלום defectively.
The base has יבקשו ('they seek') and מאת שבשמים ('from Him who is in heaven'); mss EF read תבקשו ('you seek') and add אבי ('from MY FATHER'), which Howard's English follows in parentheses.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:19): מאת] + אבי EF; יבקשו] תבקשו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And in every{H3605} place{H4725} where two{H8147} or three{H7969} join together{H2266} for my name{H8034}, there{H8033} I am{H595} among you{H8432}.

one_way_hebrew: The saying has the exact shape of the rabbinic Shekhinah-dictum: 'two who sit together and words of Torah are between them — the Shekhinah rests between them' (m. Avot 3:2, on Mal 3:16, 'they that feared YHWH spoke one with another... and YHWH hearkened'). The Hebrew Matthew and the Mishnah are speaking the same sentence-form in the same tongue; here the presence in the midst is the speaker's own — אנכי, the pronoun of Sinai's self-declaration (Exod 20:2).
שיתחברו (H2266, chavar) — 'join themselves together,' the same verb this text uses at 24:28; Greek συνηγμένοι ('gathered') loses the fellowship-root (chaver, the companion of v. 28's מחביריו).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:20): שם] omit C; בתוככם] בתוכם ABDEFG ('in THEIR midst,' as Howard's English prints '(their)').

verses.translation: Then{H227} Petros drew near{H7126} to him, saying{H559}: My lord{H113}, if my brother{H251} sins{H2398} against me, shall I forgive him up to seven{H7651} times{H6471}?

one_way_hebrew: אמחול — the forgiveness-verb throughout this chapter is מחל (vv. 21, 27, 32, 33, 35), the living Hebrew word of release (mechilah) — the term of the courts and of the Yom Kippur liturgy — not the biblical סלח. An author writes his own generation's word for forgiving a debt or a wrong; a back-translator from Greek ἀφίημι would have no reason to reach for the halakhic term five times running.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:21): פייטרוס] פיטרו A, פיטרוש BDEFG.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to him: I do not say{H559} to you up to seven{H7651}, but up to seventy{H7657}-seven{H7651}.

one_way_hebrew: שבעים ושבעה — 'seventy-seven': Lamech's number, Gen 4:24 verbatim (אם שבעתים יקם קין ולמך שבעים ושבעה) — 'if Cain is avenged sevenfold, Lamech seventy-and-sevenfold.' Vengeance's boast becomes forgiveness's measure, and only in Hebrew is the citation exact: Greek ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά is ambiguous between 'seventy-seven' and 'seventy times seven,' and the debate has run ever since. The Hebrew settles it — it is Lamech's 77, answered.
textual_notes: The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'seventy times' here — the Lamech-exact 'seventy-seven' is the Shem Tov reading.
Howard's apparatus (18:22): לו] אליו A; שבע] + פעמים EF; שבעים] שבעה D; ושבעה] + פעמים B.

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: The kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is like{H1819} a man{H120}, a king{H4428}, who sat{H3427} to make{H6213} a reckoning{H2808} with his servants{H5650} and his ministers{H8334}.

one_way_hebrew: מלכות שמים דומה לאדם מלך — the parable opens with the rabbinic mashal-formula word for word: 'to what is the matter like? to a king of flesh and blood...' (משל למלך). The Hebrew is the native genre; Greek ὡμοιώθη... ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ is its calque.
חשבון (H2808) — Qohelet's reckoning-word (Eccl 7:25,27; 9:10); a Hebrew author's natural term for the audit.
translation_notes: לאדם — the scan of Howard's text reads לאדם; the circulating transcription's לאדמ (non-final mem) is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק פ׳ (Perek 80) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (18:23): היא] הוא A, omit EF; ומשרתיו] משרתיו F.

verses.translation: And when he began{H2490} to reckon{H2803}, one{H259} came{H935} who owed{H2325} about ten{H6235} thousand{H505} gold pieces{H2091}.

greek_deviations: Greek counts in talents (μυρίων ταλάντων); the Hebrew in זהובים — gold pieces, the living coin-name of medieval Hebrew (mss ABDEF read דינרים, 'dinars'). The teller uses his own economy's money, as any native storyteller does.
translation_notes: כעשרת — 'ABOUT ten thousand' (the ms's כ of approximation); the scan reads כעשרת, and the circulating transcription's בעשרת is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:24): זהובים] דינרים ABDEF.

verses.translation: And he had nothing{H369} to give{H5414}, and his master{H113} commanded{H6680} to sell{H4376} him and his sons{H1121} and all{H3605} that was his, to repay{H7999} the money.

one_way_hebrew: The sale of the debtor and his children is the case of 2 Kgs 4:1 — 'the creditor is come to take my two sons to be bondmen' — and of Neh 5:5. The Hebrew parable stands inside the Tanakh's debt-slavery world.

ממון — mammon: the rabbinic Hebrew word for money/property (the ממון of a thousand halakhot), which the Greek gospels themselves preserve as a foreign loanword (μαμωνᾶς, Matt 6:24). Here it sits in its native tongue.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:25): ליתן] שיתן ABDEFG; ואת¹...ואת²] haplography EFG.

verses.translation: And the servant{H5650} fell{H5307} before{H6440} his master{H113} and implored{H2603} him to have compassion{H7355} on him and to wait for him, for he would repay{H7999} everything{H3605}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:26): ישלם] אשלם ABDEFG; לרחם...הכל] rewritten in ABDEFG as direct speech (לאמר חוסה עליו והמתן לי והכל).

verses.translation: And his master{H113} had pity{H2550} on him and forgave him everything{H3605}.

one_way_hebrew: ויחמול (H2550, chamal) — the sparing-pity of 2 Sam 12:4 (Nathan's parable: the rich man 'spared' — ויחמל — to take of his own flock) and Mal 3:17 ('I will spare them as a man spares his own son'). The king's pity is told in the Tanakh's sparing-verb, and the forgiving in the rabbis' מחל.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:27): אדוניו] אדוני F; vss 27-29 omitted in DG by haplography (אשלם...אשלם) — DG carry them after v. 31 instead (see v. 31 note).

verses.translation: And that servant{H5650} went out{H3318} and found{H4672} one{H259} of his fellows{H2270} who owed{H2325} him a hundred{H3967} small coins, and he seized{H2388} him and assailed{H6293} him, saying{H559}: —

one_way_hebrew: מחביריו — 'of his chaverim': the rabbinic word for one's fellows (chaver), the same root as the joining of v. 20; Greek σύνδουλος ('fellow-slave') grades by servitude, the Hebrew by fellowship — which makes the assault the uglier.
מעות — ma'ot, the rabbinic small-coin word (the מעה of the Mishnah's coin-tables); Greek has δηνάρια. Again the teller's own currency.
greek_deviations: The verse breaks off at לאמר ('saying:') — Howard's apparatus records that ALL mss, including DG, lost the words from לאמר here to לאמר in v. 29 by haplography: the demand ('Repay what you owe!') and the fellow's falling down have dropped out of the entire Hebrew family, and v. 29 opens directly with the fellow's plea.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:28): מחביריו] מחבריו AEF; בו] omit EF; לאמר] 'All mss including DG contain a haplography from לאמר (18:28) to לאמר (18:29).'

verses.translation: Have pity{H2347} on me and wait for me, and everything{H3605} I will repay{H7999}.

translation_notes: The verse is the fellow's plea; the narrative frame ('his fellow fell down and besought him, saying') fell in the haplography recorded at v. 28 — the words that survive are exactly the words the first servant himself had used (v. 26 in the majority text: חוסה עליו והמתן לי).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:29): Beginning] see note on 18:28; והכל] + לו B.

verses.translation: But he was not willing{H14} to listen{H8085} to him, and he led him{H1980} to the prison-house{H5470}, until he repaid{H7999} him everything{H3605}.

one_way_hebrew: בית הסוהר — the Tanakh's one named prison: Joseph's (בית הסהר, Gen 39:20-23; 40:3,5 — seven times, and nowhere else in Scripture). The unforgiving creditor casts his fellow into the very house where the innocent Joseph lay. Greek φυλακή is any jail; the Hebrew is Joseph's.
ולא אבה לשמוע — the fixed refusal-formula (Deut 13:9; Judg 19:25, לא אבו לשמע).
translation_notes: ויוליכוהו — plural in form ('they led him') where sense is singular; Howard prints '(he).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:30): ויוליכוהו] ויוליכהו ABDEFG; שלם] ישלם A; לו²] omit ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And the servants{H5650} of the king{H4428} saw{H7200} what he did{H6213}, and it angered{H2734} them greatly{H3966}, and they came{H935} and told{H5046} their master{H113}.

one_way_hebrew: ויחר להם מאד — the anger-idiom of Gen 4:5 (ויחר לקין מאד) and Jonah 4:1; Greek ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα ('were very sorry') softens what the Hebrew burns.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:31): את] omit BDEFG; עשה] + vss 27-29 DG — mss D and G, having lost vv. 27-29 in their place, carry them here.

verses.translation: Then{H227} his master{H113} called{H7121} him and said{H559} to him: Cursed{H779} servant{H5650}! Did I not forgive you all{H3605} your debts{H2326} when you appeased me?

one_way_hebrew: פייסתני — 'you APPEASED me': the rabbinic verb פייס (piyyes), the technical term of reconciliation between man and fellow — the very word of the Mishnah's rule that Yom Kippur does not atone 'until he appeases (שירצה/יפייס) his fellow' (m. Yoma 8:9). The parable's vocabulary is the halakha's own; Greek παρεκάλεσάς με ('you entreated me') has no such institution behind it.
חוב (H2326) — 'debt': Ezek 18:7's word (חבלתו חוב ישיב, the debtor's pledge restored) and the rabbis' standing term for obligation.
greek_deviations: עבד ארור — 'CURSED servant' — where Greek has 'wicked servant' (δοῦλε πονηρέ): the Hebrew speaks the covenant curse-word (ארור, Deut 27-28's refrain) over the unforgiving.
translation_notes: קרא — the scan of Howard's text reads קרא ('called'); the circulating transcription's פרא is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:32): חוביך] חובך ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And why{H4069} did you not forgive your servant{H5650} when he implored{H2603} you, as I forgave you?

translation_notes: לעבדך — 'YOUR servant': the base text makes the fellow the creditor's own servant in the asking; ms B reads לחברך ('your fellow'), matching v. 28's מחביריו and the Greek σύνδουλον.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:33): לעבדך] לחברך B, לעבדיך A.

verses.translation: And the anger{H639} of his master{H113} burned{H2734} against him, and he commanded{H6680} to afflict him{H6031} until he should repay{H7999} all{H3605} the debt{H2326}.

one_way_hebrew: ויחר אף — the Torah's full wrath-idiom (ויחר אף יהוה, Exod 4:14 and throughout); Greek ὀργισθείς is one word where the Hebrew burns by formula.
לענותו (H6031, anah) — 'to afflict him': the oppression-verb of Exod 1:11-12; Greek has the professional βασανισταί ('torturers') — the Hebrew names the affliction, not the guild.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:34): לו] omit A; ויצו] ויאמר G.

verses.translation: So{H3651} will my Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064} do{H6213} to you, if you do not forgive — each man{H376} his brother{H251} — with a whole{H8003} heart{H3820}.

one_way_hebrew: בלב שלם — 'with a WHOLE heart': David's charge to Solomon (1 Chr 28:9, בלב שלם ובנפש חפצה) and the recurring measure of true service (1 Kgs 8:61). Greek ἀπὸ τῶν καρδιῶν ὑμῶν ('from your hearts') has the organ but not the wholeness — the Hebrew demands the undivided heart of the Shema in the act of forgiving.
איש את אחיו — 'each man his brother': the Torah's distributive idiom (Exod 32:27), closing the chapter where it began — the brother of v. 15.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (18:35): בלב] בלבב A.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 18 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is the community-discipline chapter written in the community's own legal Hebrew. (1) 18:17 sentences the unrepentant to be regarded כמנודה — 'as one BANNED,' the rabbinic niddui — where Greek has 'as the gentile and the tax-collector'; and the hearing is בקהל, the Torah's assembly (Deut 23), where Greek says ἐκκλησία — the same Greek word that at 16:18 covered בית תפלתי: the Hebrew distinguishes what the Greek merges. (2) 18:18 gives the binding-loosing in the halakhic pair itself — תאסרו/תתירו (issur/hetter) — in the plural, where 16:19's grant to Shimon was singular; the unpointed אלה reads 'these' or 'oath' (Howard: 'every oath which you bind'), making the verse Num 30's vow-law in the second reading. (3) 18:15's private rebuke is Lev 19:17's own verb (הוכיחנו), addressed by name to Shimon called Petros — no addressee in the Greek — and ends 'you have ACQUIRED (קנית) your brother.' (4) 18:22 answers Lamech exactly: שבעים ושבעה, Gen 4:24's 'seventy-seven' — vengeance's number remade as forgiveness's; the Greek's ambiguous 'seventy times seven' debate does not exist in Hebrew (Vat. Ebr. 100 reads 'seventy times'). (5) The forgiveness-verb throughout (vv. 21-35) is the rabbinic מחל (mechilah), and 18:32's פייסתני ('when you APPEASED me') is m. Yoma 8:9's own reconciliation term; the coins are זהובים and מעות, the mashal opens with the rabbinic king-parable formula, and the debtor goes to Joseph's בית הסוהר (Gen 39:20). (6) 18:6 kills the offender with Judg 9:53's פלח רכב and drowns him in Mic 7:19's מצולות ים — where the sins go; 18:12-14's sheep run on Ezek 34:16's pair, the driven-away (נדחה) and the lost (אבד). (7) 18:10 forbids JUDGING the little ones (תדינו; Greek 'despising') whose messengers see 'the SONS of my Father' (בני; nearly all mss assimilate to פני, 'the face,' with the Greek). (8) 18:11 reads 'the Son of Man has CEASED (בטל) to save THE ENEMIES (האויבים)' — one letter from האובדים, 'the lost'; BDEFG read בא ('has come'); Vat. Ebr. 100 lacks the verse with the earliest Greek witnesses. (9) 18:19 conditions answered prayer on two who 'desire to set PEACE on earth' (לשים שלום) — Greek's συμφωνήσωσιν ('agree') reads like a rendering of the shalom-idiom. (10) The chapter's text-history is visibly Hebrew: 18:2b-5a lost by haplography (נער אחד...נער אחד) in all mss but A; 18:4 lost in all; 18:28b-29a lost in all (לאמר...לאמר); 18:27-29 displaced after v. 31 in DG — scribal accidents that happen between Hebrew words. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 77), 12 (78), 15 (79 — misprinted פקר), and 23 (80). Forgiveness closes בלב שלם, 'with a whole heart' (1 Chr 28:9).
